78	func humanateBytes(s uint64, base float64, minDigits int, sizes []string) string {
79		if s < 10 {
80			return fmt.Sprintf("%d B", s)
81		}
82		e := math.Floor(logn(float64(s), base))
83		suffix := sizes[int(e)]
84		val := float64(s) / math.Pow(base, e)
85	
86		// Determine how many decimal places to keep based on the unrounded
87		// value's integer-digit count, then round exactly once to that
88		// precision. Rounding first to a fixed precision and then again when
89		// formatting (double rounding) can flip the result at a boundary due
90		// to floating point error (see #103).
91		intDigits := countDigits(int64(val))
92		digits := max(minDigits-intDigits, 0)
93		rounding := math.Pow10(digits)
94		val = math.Floor(val*rounding+0.5) / rounding
95	
96		// Rounding may have carried into an additional integer digit (e.g.
97		// 9.996 -> 10.0), which means fewer decimal places should be shown
98		// than originally computed.
99		if newIntDigits := countDigits(int64(val)); newIntDigits > intDigits {
100			digits = max(digits-(newIntDigits-intDigits), 0)
101		}

103		ff := "%%.%df %%s"
104		f := fmt.Sprintf(ff, digits)

161	// ParseBytes("42 mib") -> 44040192, nil
162	func ParseBytes(s string) (uint64, error) {
163		lastDigit := 0
164		hasComma := false
165		for _, r := range s {
166			if !(unicode.IsDigit(r) || r == '.' || r == ',') {
167				break
168			}
169			if r == ',' {
170				hasComma = true
171			}
172			lastDigit++
173		}
174	
175		num := s[:lastDigit]
176		if hasComma {
177			num = strings.Replace(num, ",", "", -1)
178		}
179	
180		f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(num, 64)
181		if err != nil {
182			return 0, err
183		}
184

186		if m, ok := bytesSizeTable[extra]; ok {

188			// integers above 2^53, and the multiplication below would also reject

190			// uint64 arithmetic with an overflow check.

101			return input, ""
102		}
103		mag := math.Abs(input)
104		exponent := math.Floor(logn(mag, 10))
105		exponent = math.Floor(exponent/3) * 3
106	
107		// Outside the table there is no prefix that can name the magnitude, so
108		// clamp to the nearest one there is and let the returned value carry the
109		// remaining orders of magnitude. Without this the lookup below misses,
110		// the prefix comes back as the empty string, and the value is left scaled
111		// for a prefix that was never returned - so the caller silently gets a
112		// number off by as much as 10^300 with no error.
113		if exponent < minSIExponent {
114			exponent = minSIExponent
115		} else if exponent > maxSIExponent {
116			exponent = maxSIExponent
117		}
118	
119		value := mag / math.Pow(10, exponent)

122		// Should return 1 M instead of 1000 k

124			exponent += 3

154	// ParseBigBytes("42 mib") -> 44040192, nil
155	func ParseBigBytes(s string) (*big.Int, error) {
156		lastDigit := 0
157		hasComma := false
158		for _, r := range s {
159			if !(unicode.IsDigit(r) || r == '.' || r == ',') {
160				break
161			}
162			if r == ',' {
163				hasComma = true
164			}
165			lastDigit++
166		}
167	
168		num := s[:lastDigit]
169		if hasComma {
170			num = strings.Replace(num, ",", "", -1)
171		}
172	
173		val := &big.Rat{}
174		_, err := fmt.Sscanf(num, "%f", val)
175		if err != nil {

177		}

180		if m, ok := bigBytesSizeTable[extra]; ok {
181			mv := (&big.Rat{}).SetInt(m)
182			val.Mul(val, mv)
183			rv := &big.Int{}
184			rv.Div(val.Num(), val.Denom())
185			return rv, nil
186		}

188		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unhandled size name: %v", extra)
